name: Italy
proverbs: A calm sea never made a skilled sailor.
He who goes slowly, goes safely and goes far.
Love and a cough cannot be hidden.
At the end of the game, the king and the pawn go into the same box.
Between saying and doing lies a great sea.

name: Japan
proverbs: Fall seven times, stand up eight.
Even monkeys fall from trees.
The nail that sticks out gets hammered down.
A frog in a well does not know the great ocean.
One kind word can warm three winter months.

name: France
proverbs: Appetite comes while eating.
Little by little, the bird builds its nest.
Impossible is not a word in our language.
The night brings good counsel.
You cannot make an omelet without breaking eggs.

name: United States
proverbs: The early bird catches the worm.
A penny saved is a penny earned.
Do not count your chickens before they hatch.
The squeaky wheel gets the grease.
Actions speak louder than words.

name: United Kingdom
proverbs: A watched pot never boils.
Every cloud has a silver lining.
A stitch in time saves nine.
Still waters run deep.
Do not put all your eggs in one basket.

name: Germany
proverbs: The morning hour has gold in its mouth.
Practice makes the master.
All beginnings are difficult.
Better a sparrow in the hand than a pigeon on the roof.
Lies have short legs.

name: Spain
proverbs: Into a closed mouth, no flies can enter.
Tell me who you walk with, and I will tell you who you are.
A shrimp that falls asleep is swept away by the current.
To a good listener, few words are needed.
Even if a monkey dresses in silk, it remains a monkey.

name: China
proverbs: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
The best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago; the second best time is now.
Do not be afraid of growing slowly; be afraid only of standing still.
Dig the well before you are thirsty.
A diamond cannot be polished without friction.

name: India
proverbs: You cannot clap with one hand.
When you live in the river, do not make an enemy of the crocodile.
The tree laden with fruit always bends low.
A guest is akin to God.
Drops of water together fill the earthen pot.

name: Brazil
proverbs: Soft water strikes hard stone until it drills a hole.
He who has no dog hunts with a cat.
The parrot eats the corn, while the parakeet takes the fame.
From grain to grain, the hen fills its belly.
A gourd floating downstream never knows what waits ahead.

name: Mexico
proverbs: With a full belly comes a happy heart.
He who leans against a good tree finds good shade.
If the sky rains lemons, learn to make lemonade.
Even the best hunter loses a hare now and then.
Where there is smoke, fire was lit.

name: Egypt
proverbs: Man fears time, yet time fears the pyramids.
An old friend is worth more than new gold.
The winds do not always blow as the ships desire.
He who fears his own shadow cannot walk in the sun.
A monkey in the eyes of its mother is a gazelle.

name: Turkey
proverbs: Drop by drop, a lake is formed.
No matter how far you have gone on a wrong road, turn back.
A cup of coffee is remembered for forty years.
A rolling stone gathers no moss, yet working iron shines.
One hand washes the other, and both wash the face.

name: Greece
proverbs: A society grows great when old men plant trees whose shade they shall never sit in.
One swallow does not bring the spring.
The beginning is half of the whole.
Slowly, slowly the sour grape becomes honey.
Know thyself before judging another.

name: Russia
proverbs: Measure seven times, cut once.
Trust, but verify.
If you chase two hares, you will catch neither.
The first pancake always turns out lumpy.
The quieter you go, the farther you will get.

name: Canada
proverbs: A good neighbor is better than a distant cousin.
You miss every shot you do not take.
Paddle your own canoe when the river widens.
Winter always asks what summer has done.
A canoe cannot move forward if two paddlers row in opposite ways.

name: Australia
proverbs: We are all visitors to this time and place, just passing through.
Keep your face to the sunshine and the shadows fall behind.
A fair go makes mates out of strangers.
Do not wait for a calm tide to mend your boat.
Those who lose dreaming are lost.

name: South Korea
proverbs: Even a sheet of paper is lighter when lifted together.
Start is half the battle.
A tiger leaves its hide behind, a person leaves their name.
Words without feet travel a thousand miles.
After hardship comes sweetness.

name: Argentina
proverbs: Brothers must be united, for that is the first law.
To a barking dog, throw no stone; keep riding.
Do not trade a horse in the middle of the river.
A bird in the hand is worth a hundred flying.
He who gets burned with milk blows even on cold cream.

name: Thailand
proverbs: When the water rises, hurry to scoop it.
Do not ride an elephant just to catch a grasshopper.
Walk slowly and you will catch a big knife-handle.
One rotten fish spoils the whole basket.
Speak silver, stay silent for gold.

name: Sweden
proverbs: There is no bad weather, only bad clothing.
Fear less, hope more; eat less, chew more.
A shared joy is a double joy; a shared sorrow is half a sorrow.
Better to flee poorly than to fight poorly.
Who waits for something good never waits too long.

name: South Africa
proverbs: A person is a person through other people.
When the roots are deep, there is no reason to fear the wind.
A roaring lion kills no game.
Sticks in a bundle are unbreakable.
However long the night, the dawn will break.

name: Portugal
proverbs: Grain by grain, the hen fills its crop.
Who does not risk does not eat.
A barking dog does not bite.
Water that does not move grows stagnant.
Behind the mountains there are still more mountains.

name: Netherlands
proverbs: Tall trees catch much wind.
Do not sell the bear's skin before the bear is shot.
Even if you give a monkey a golden ring, it stays an ugly thing.
Who has butter on their head should stay out of the sun.
The best captains always stand ashore.

name: Poland
proverbs: Not my circus, not my monkeys.
A guest in the house is God in the house.
Without work there are no sweet cakes.
What is too much is not healthy.
Hope is the mother of fools, yet every wise soul keeps it.

name: Norway
proverbs: Do not sell the skin before the bear is caught.
He who whispers lies.
Many small streams make a great river.
Even a small hill looks like a mountain to a tiny ant.
A burnt child shuns the fire.

name: Ireland
proverbs: A good laugh and a long sleep are the two best cures.
It is in the shelter of each other that people live.
The longest road out is the shortest road home.
A silent mouth is sweet to hear.
Beware the anger of a patient soul.

name: Switzerland
proverbs: Speech is silver, silence is golden.
No money, no mercenary.
You cannot have both the five-cent coin and the bread roll.
Mountains never meet, yet people always do.
Even the steepest summit is climbed step by step.

name: Austria
proverbs: Nothing is eaten as hot as it is cooked.
When two people argue, the third rejoices.
Better an egg today than a hen tomorrow.
Every pot finds its own lid.
Small gifts preserve long friendships.

name: Ukraine
proverbs: Without a willow and a viburnum tree, there is no homeland.
The eyes are afraid, yet the hands still do the work.
A word is not a sparrow; once it flies out, you cannot catch it.
Measure your coat according to your cloth.
A friendly word is like a warm spring day.

name: Morocco
proverbs: Little by little, the camel enters the cooking pot.
A bird in the hand is better than ten on the tree.
He who wants honey must bear the stings of bees.
Do not open a door you cannot close.
The tongue has no bone, yet it breaks bones.

name: Kenya
proverbs: Hurry, hurry has no blessing.
When elephants fight, it is the grass that suffers.
Treat the earth well; it was lent to you by your children.
One finger cannot kill a louse.
Even the best swimmer can be carried by the river.

name: Nigeria
proverbs: A child who washes his hands well may dine with kings.
Not to know is bad; not to wish to know is worse.
However far a stream flows, it never forgets its source.
He who brings kola nut brings life.
When the moon is not full, the stars shine more brightly.

name: Ethiopia
proverbs: When spider webs unite, they can tie up a lion.
He who conceals his disease cannot expect to be cured.
Coffee is our bread.
Fifty lemons are a load for one person, yet a perfume for fifty.
A fool and water will go the way they are diverted.

name: Vietnam
proverbs: When eating a fruit, remember who planted the tree.
Traveling one day teaches a basketful of wisdom.
A single tree cannot make a forest, yet three trees together make a high mountain.
Near ink you turn black; near a lamp you turn bright.
Failure is the mother of success.

name: Indonesia
proverbs: Still water often hides deep currents.
Step by step, a hill becomes a mountain.
There is no ivory without a crack.
Like a frog beneath a coconut shell.
Where the earth is stepped on, there the sky is upheld.

name: Philippines
proverbs: He who does not look back to where he came from will never reach his destination.
If you plant wind, you will harvest a storm.
No matter how long the procession, it still returns to the church.
A broom is sturdy because its strands are tightly bound.
Even a hard stone wears away under steady drops of rain.

name: Iran
proverbs: Do not cut down the tree that gives you shade.
One hand makes no sound on its own.
With patience, sour grapes turn into sweet halva.
A wall has mice, and mice have ears.
Even if the night is pitch black, morning is near.

name: Saudi Arabia
proverbs: Choose the neighbor before the house, and the companion before the road.
He who fears climbing mountains will live forever in the hollows.
A camel does not see the crookedness of its own neck.
Patience is the key to relief.
The desert teaches you to value every single drop.

name: Colombia
proverbs: Never give papaya—do not leave yourself an easy target.
Better alone than in bad company.
To a stubborn mule, give a quiet rider.
Every rooster crows loudest on its own hillside.
He who wakes early finds help on the trail.

name: Peru
proverbs: No matter how tall the mountain, the path finds a way around it.
Do not steal, do not lie, do not be lazy.
Into the nest of a sleeping bird blows the wind.
The condor flies high, yet never forgets to look at the earth.
A burden shared together does not bend the shoulder.

name: Chile
proverbs: The cord always breaks at its thinnest thread.
In a blacksmith's house, the knife is made of wood.
Little by little, the traveler crosses the high pass.
Do not ask the elm tree to bear pears.
Good wine needs no loud crier.

name: Cuba
proverbs: You cannot cover the sun with a single finger.
The shrimp that sleeps is carried out by the tide.
If you do not have a horse, ride your own courage.
Every palm tree bends in the hurricane, yet stands again.
He who sings scares his sorrows away.

name: New Zealand
proverbs: Turn your face to the sun and the shadows fall behind you.
Seek the treasure you value most dearly; if you bow your head, let it be to a lofty mountain.
With your food basket and my food basket, the people will thrive.
A single frond breaks easily, yet woven flax holds fast.
Although it is small, it is made of greenstone.

name: Iceland
proverbs: It will all work out in the end.
Bare is the back of a brotherless man.
Better to walk barefoot than without a book.
Do not praise the day before evening.
A small spark can awaken a sleeping hearth.

name: Finland
proverbs: Even through a grey stone, persistence finds a way.
Who reaches for the spruce tree tumbles into the juniper.
Work praises its maker.
Better a titmouse in the palm than ten on a branch.
In the sauna, anger melts like snow.

name: Czechia
proverbs: As many languages as you know, as many times you are a human being.
Without work, there are no sweet pastries.
Golden hands earn bread anywhere.
Who digs a pit for another falls into it himself.
A good deed returns when least expected.

name: Hungary
proverbs: More was lost on the battlefield than a single setback.
Do not look a gift horse in the mouth.
Whoever searches will eventually find.
A bird is known by its feathers, a person by their friends.
Appetite grows when the cauldron simmers.

name: Romania
proverbs: Water passes, yet the stones remain.
Build your sled in summer and your cart in winter.
A sweet word brings much closer.
Good deeds are like seeds sown along the road.
He who rises early reaches farther.

name: Croatia
proverbs: Praise the sea, yet hold tight to the shore.
Agreement builds a house, discord tears it down.
A quiet river hollows out the deepest bank.
What you sow in youth, you harvest in age.
An old olive tree still gives oil to patient hands.

name: Georgia
proverbs: A guest is a gift from God.
What you give away is yours forever; what you keep is lost.
A good horse never grows tired on a long road.
One tree cannot hold back the mountain wind.
Truth moves slowly, yet it always arrives.

name: Kazakhstan
proverbs: A horse is the wings of a rider.
Where there is unity, there is prosperity.
Knowledge is an inexhaustible spring.
A bird returns to the nest where it grew its feathers.
Respect for elders opens every yurt door.

name: Uzbekistan
proverbs: The guest is greater than your own father.
A tree flourishes in one place; a stone grows weighty where it rests.
Even a long caravan follows a single bell.
Kind words lure even a snake from its burrow.
A garden blooms when its keeper does not sleep.

name: Mongolia
proverbs: A good horse is tested on a long journey; a good friend is tested in hardship.
It is better to travel and see once than to hear a hundred times.
The sky has no pillars, yet it never falls.
Even a distant mountain can be reached by a steady rider.
A loose rope tangles the whole herd.

name: Nepal
proverbs: Even the highest peak begins beneath your feet.
A monkey cannot appreciate the taste of ginger.
Where there is a will, even stone yields a path.
Do not forget the bridge after crossing the gorge.
A lamp sheds no light directly beneath its own base.

name: Sri Lanka
proverbs: A crab only walks straight in its own imagination.
When the branch bends, the fruit is ripe.
Do not throw stones at a hive when you have no shelter.
Even the smallest cinnamon bark perfumes the whole pot.
A bird perched on a fragile branch trusts its wings, not the twig.

name: Malaysia
proverbs: Little by little, over time it becomes a mountain.
Like a frog under a coconut shell, mistaking the dark for the whole sky.
Heavy loads are carried together; light loads are lifted together.
If you do not crack the bamboo shoot, you will never taste the core.
When the river rises, the boat rises with it.

name: Jordan
proverbs: A tent stands firm only when its pegs hold together.
Hospitality begins with a smile and a fresh pot of cardamom coffee.
Ask someone who has walked the road, not just the scholar.
The stone you reject may become the cornerstone of the arch.
A quiet brook waters more fields than a sudden flood.

name: Ghana
proverbs: It is not wrong to go back and fetch what you forgot.
Wisdom is like a baobab tree; no one person can embrace it alone.
By the time the fool has learned the game, the players have dispersed.
One head alone does not go into council.
A bird that flies off the earth and lands on an anthill is still on the ground.

name: Senegal
proverbs: A person is the medicine of another person.
Patience can cook a stone.
No matter how long a log stays in the river, it never becomes a crocodile.
He who asks questions does not lose his way.
The eye sees far, yet it cannot see itself.

name: Tanzania
proverbs: Little by little fills the measure.
Unity is strength; division is weakness.
A boat does not go forward if each one rows their own way.
When two bulls lock horns, the grass beneath pays the price.
An axe forgets, yet the tree remembers.

name: Madagascar
proverbs: Do not kick away the canoe that helped you cross the river.
Cross the river in a crowd and the crocodile will not eat you.
Words are like eggs; once hatched, they grow wings.
Even a thin thread can mend a wide cloth when doubled.
Look at the chameleon: one eye on the past, one eye on the future.

name: Tunisia
proverbs: An olive tree planted by your grandfather feeds your grandchildren.
Do not judge the sea while standing on dry sand.
If the wind rises, build a windmill rather than a wall.
A sweet tongue opens iron gates.
Better a steady lantern than a brief flash of lightning.

name: Ecuador
proverbs: He who does not dare to cross the mist never sees the summit.
Every volcano sleeps until its own hour.
Good cacao takes patience before it becomes sweet.
The condor needs both wings to ride the valley wind.
Small seeds grow tall when the rain is shared.

name: Uruguay
proverbs: Even the longest road begins outside your front gate.
Do not rush the kettle when sharing mate with friends.
A good horse knows its rider by the lightness of the hand.
Storms pass quickly over open plains.
Quiet water mirrors the clearest sky.

name: Bolivia
proverbs: The mountain does not hurry, yet rivers carve their paths from it.
Share your salt and you will never travel alone.
A llama carries only what its stride can bear.
High air clears the mind and steadies the step.
Weave two threads together and the poncho lasts a lifetime.
